text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
All Albanian newspapers report events in southern town of Vlore, theatre of violent clashes between police riots and demonstrators.
KOHA JONE
- The daily says President Sali Berisha's police killed three people in Vlore where a 5,000-strong force failed to crack down on thousands of demonstrators protesting against his government.
- Main opposition Forum for Democracy alliance called on Berisha to stop violence and terror immediately against politicians and journalists.
- The family of Artur Rustemi, a protester killed in Vlore on Monday, is quoted as saying "Berisha's democracy killed our son and brother".
- The paper says students and jobless people have become riot police after promises they would be given $400 per month.
- The "leek government" of Aleksander Meksi, a reference to use of the vegetable by protesters, should quit as soon as possible, Vlore protesters say.
- Berisha is all but a "Moslim fundamentalist", paper says.
- Parliamentarians of the ruling Democratic Party back Meksi's request for state of emergency in Vlore.
- Protests could spread throughout the country if Berisha orders the army to deploy.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Meksi wants the army in Vlore, considering it the only means of guarding state institutions.
- Some of the ruling party politicians have asked for Meksi's government dismissal.
- The Forum for Democracy will hold a rally in Tirana on Wednesday though police turned down its request.
- Parliament is to discuss a draft law on a state of emergency in Vlore to halt further protests.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- The ruling Democratic Party is killing Vlore and provoking a civil war in the country..
- The state of law in Albanian is becoming a police state.
- Two-page report on situation in Albania viewed by foreign press.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Meksi rejected calls for his government's resignation, saying Albania needed firm rule in such a dificult situation.
- Prominent writer Ismail Kadare calls on all polticians to abandon their differences and reach a common view to help the country out of deadlock.
